title: 2020 Taiwan Cultural Content Industry Survey Report, Vol. 4: Games and Esports
methodology: Industry survey/reconstruction: 98 game companies, split into 46 game developers and 52 agents/publishers; esports was tabulated separately.
assessment: Primary government-affiliated industry survey. Retain 9,047 as game-only surveyed-company employees. Do not add the separate 660 esports employees without an explicit combined series.
next_step: Obtain the Chinese original/appendix if a sample-frame, response-rate, or fieldwork-date citation is needed.

title: 2022 Taiwan Cultural Content Industry Survey Report: Games and Immersive Interactive Games
methodology: Survey list of 200 companies; 133 ultimately surveyed. Employee counts from company responses, with missing open responses supplemented by 104 Job Bank public records where available.
assessment: Primary government-affiliated report. Retain 9,929 as an observed/reconstructed respondent-frame employee count, not national employment or FTE. Its active-company sampling may bias results upward.
next_step: Use the report's p. 11 and p. 7 scope/method caveats in any published methodology note.

title: 2023 Taiwan Cultural Content Industry Survey Report: Games and Esports
methodology: Newer game/esports industry report with company and employee-composition material; a comparable total game-employee count was not located in its searchable text during this bounded pass.
assessment: Authoritative follow-up source but not a retained observation. Do not infer a total from employee age/composition charts.
next_step: Download/inspect tables and chart data manually, then verify whether any total is game-only, esports-only, or combined.

title: Digital Content Industry Yearbooks download catalogue
publisher: Taipei Computer Association (hosting official MOEA/MODA yearbooks)
methodology: Annual industry yearbooks: MOEA Industrial Development Bureau through 2021; Ministry of Digital Affairs Administration for Digital Industries thereafter; compiled by the Institute for Information Industry.
assessment: Authoritative continuity/definition source, but its stated coverage is broad digital content rather than games alone. No compatible game-employment observation retained.
next_step: Extract specific yearbook tables only if they explicitly identify game-only headcount and methodology.

title: Digital Content Industry manpower supply-demand projection
methodology: Forward manpower-demand projection covering five digital-content fields including digital games, animation, audiovisual applications, digital publishing/archives, and digital learning.
assessment: Do not use as game employment: it is a broader multi-subsector forecast, not an observed game headcount.
next_step: Retrieve report only for a separately-labelled digital-content forecast series, if needed.

title: Industry Classification: 5821 Digital Game Software Publishing
publisher: Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Taiwan
methodology: Classification definition: digital-game software publishing, publisher-operated online games and publishing intermediaries; commissioned game development without publishing belongs elsewhere (6211).
assessment: Useful exclusion rule. A 5821 administrative series would omit non-publishing game developers, therefore cannot substitute for the TAICCA game-industry frame.
next_step: If administrative employment is needed, test coverage of both 5821 and 6211 and document the unavoidable non-game software contamination in 6211.
